## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Rewrite unresolvable internal_url when casting

#### Background:
Chromecast devices tend to ignore DNS servers supplied by DHCP, and instead reverts to Google's DNS servers.
This tends to break casting of media served from `internal_url`, e.g. TTS messages.

#### Solution:
To improve resolve any media_url served from `internal_url` if it's not publicly resolvable and replace with the IP address before passing it to ChromeCast.
This will break any vhost configuration, so the URL is only rewritten when not publicly resolvable.
An alternative would be to rewrite to use `external_url`, but that will not work for users with incorrectly configured NAT loopback.

I don't see why this needs to be added? TTS can be overwritten already if needed by the user.
Even this is not solving it. For example, on my network, this will instantly fail, for multiple reasons.

If any of this is added, we should add these kinds of capabilities centrally, not specific in an integration.

Thanks for reviewing, and I agree with the conclusion that this will break more than it will solve.

Clearly https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tts#base_url is good enough.

issue_context.title: Google Cast - TTS URL: Prefer External over Internal

  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
When casting TTS messages, the internal URL is currently being preferred over the external URL.  The problem with this, is if the internal URL is not publicly resolvable, the cast message is ignored.  More specifically, this is an issue when the internal URL is using a hostname that is resolvable to the internal network, but not publicly resolvable, rather than using an IP address.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.113.3
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): unknown exactly, but i imagine around the time the base_url was replaced with external and internal urls.
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core):  Hass.io / HassOS 4.11 / Supervisor 229
- Integration causing this issue: Google Cast
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cast/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
homeassistant:
  ...
  external_url: https://home.domain.com
  internal_url: http://hassio.domain.com:8123
```

## Additional information
1. When using an internal IP for the internal URL address (http://192.168.1.1:8123): Casting Works
2. When using the external host name, which is publicly resolvable as internal URL (https://home.domain.com): Casting Works
3. When using the internal host name, which is not publicly resolvable (http://hassio.domain.com:8123): Casting Fails

If both an external and internal URL are provided.  It should be reasonably presumed that the internal URL is not public, but is private and not accessible via the internet.  In this case, the external URL should be preferred over the internal.

The problem is, that you cannot assume the external URL is available either. Especially for people with NAT loopback issue, which is, unfortunately, a large group as well.

Is there some form of test that can be implemented:

```txt
If both external and internal urls are configured then
  If internal url is not resolvable then
    Use external url
  Else
    Use internal Url
  End
End
```

Hey there @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`cast`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L71) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@thewilliambond That sounds simple, but Home Assistant will be able to resolve itself on its internal URL. Hence, that check will always result in the internal URL.

The base URL of things like the `cast` integration can be overridden if you need to.

The root cause is that the chromecasts insist on using Google's DNS servers.
Maybe a simple solution would be to resolve the url ourselves, and replace the hostname with the resolved IP? That could be done in either the cast integration or in pychromecast.

Edit: In the cast integration, we can check if the hostname matches `internal_url`, and if it does we resolve it ourselves.
That sounds reasonable as well and might be better than exposing the host name in the first place if it isn't absolutely necessary.

> Maybe a simple solution would be to resolve the url ourselves, and replace the hostname with the resolved IP? That could be done in either the cast integration or in pychromecast.

That won't work if a TLS connection is required ~(and as far as I know, that is required for Cast)~ as this will break SNI.

@hmmbob Cast does not require media to be served over TLS. Anyhow the idea was not good and you're right that it would break if the `homeassistant.internal_url` or `tts.base_url` are using TLS or a vhost, and probably for other reasons as well.
Better ideas might be to:
- Warn the user at startup if cast is enabled and `internal_url` or `tts.base_url` can't be resolved through Google's DNS servers
- Warn if media served from `homeassistant.internal_url` or `tts.base_url` doesn't play
I wonder if we should test at startup if our external url is resolvable from Home Assistant. If it is, prefer it over internal url.
@balloob That will not work, as you cannot assume the HA instance has the same level of access or network properties.
Right. But in case we can access it, it's nice to know so we can use that knowledge.
I actually had a discussion with @emontnemery on Discord. The best way to check, IMHO, is to know if the TTS file is actually picked up by the player.

There's no agreement on having Cast or TTS prefer the external URL or having the Cast integration rewrite the URLs.
This problem is improved a bit by #38603 as tts casting will no longer silently fail.

review_comments: So what if someone is using a separate subnet with firewalls? This assumes Home Assistant has the same level of access as the cast devices (or the other way around).

This assumes one is using a local resolver on their HA installation, which doesn't have to be the case (e.g., OS installations use their own resolvers, which may have been failed over. Or when using a split DNS setup, where HA is configured to use external DNS to avoid a DNS loop, it will cause to resolve externally all of a sudden and return an external IP)
